summary.text: Paris is the capital and largest city of France, set on the Seine in the Île-de-France region. It is often called the City of Light, a nickname tied to its leading role in the Age of Enlightenment.

facts.label: Population
facts.value: About 2.04 million people live in the city proper (January 2026 estimate), within a metropolitan area of roughly 13.3 million (2023).

facts.label: Area
facts.value: The city covers about 105.4 square kilometres.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Lies on the Seine in the centre of the Île-de-France region.

facts.label: Nickname
facts.value: Known as the "City of Light", mainly because of its leading role in the Age of Enlightenment.

media.alt: The Eiffel Tower rising above the rooftops of Paris, seen from the Tour Saint-Jacques with the Seine and its bridges in view.
media.attribution: Yann Caradec, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons — La Tour Eiffel vue de la Tour Saint-Jacques, Paris août 2014 (2).jpg

summary.text: London is the capital and largest city of England and the United Kingdom, standing on the River Thames in the southeast of England. Founded by the Romans as Londinium, it has been a major settlement for nearly 2,000 years.

facts.label: Population
facts.value: About 9.14 million people in 2025, with a wider metropolitan area of 15.4 million, the largest in Western Europe.

facts.label: Origins
facts.value: The City of London was founded by the Romans as Londinium and has kept its medieval boundaries.

facts.label: River
facts.value: Stands on the Thames, at the head of a 50-mile (80 km) tidal estuary running down to the North Sea.

facts.label: Government
facts.value: The City of Westminster has been the site of the national government and parliament for centuries.

media.alt: The London skyline at sunset, with the River Thames, Tower Bridge and the financial district's towers seen from above.
media.attribution: Ilya Grigorik, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

summary.text: The Sagrada Família is a Catholic basilica still under construction in the Eixample district of Barcelona, Spain. Designed by the architect Antoni Gaudí, it is the tallest church in the world.

facts.label: Architect
facts.value: Designed by the Spanish architect Antoni Gaudí.

facts.label: Consecration
facts.value: Pope Benedict XVI consecrated the church and proclaimed it a basilica on 7 November 2010.

facts.label: Height
facts.value: It is the tallest church in the world.

facts.label: World Heritage
facts.value: In 2005, parts of the building were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site under "Works of Antoni Gaudí".

media.alt: Exterior of the Sagrada Família in Barcelona, showing the carved stone sculpture of its Passion Facade.
media.attribution: Reda Kerbush, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons — Exterior of the Sagrada Família.jpg

summary.text: The Alhambra is a palace and fortress complex in Granada, Spain. It is among the best-known monuments of Islamic architecture and also holds notable examples of Spanish Renaissance architecture.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Granada, Spain.

facts.label: Type
facts.value: A palace and fortress complex.

facts.label: Rarity
facts.value: It is described as the only well-preserved palace from the medieval Islamic world.

media.alt: The Palace of Charles V within the Alhambra complex in Granada at dawn, seen from a viewpoint across the valley.

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons — Dawn Charles V Palace Alhambra Granada Andalusia Spain.jpg

summary.text: The Palace of Versailles is a château and historic monument in the Yvelines department of France, southwest of Paris. It served as the principal residence of the French kings Louis XIV, Louis XV and Louis XVI.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: In Versailles, in the Yvelines department, southwest of Paris.

facts.label: Royal residence
facts.value: The principal residence of Louis XIV, Louis XV and Louis XVI.

facts.label: Type
facts.value: A château and historic monument.

media.alt: Aerial view of the Palace of Versailles and its formal gardens in France.
media.attribution: ToucanWings, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons — Versailles Palace (FRA) – Equestrian Olympic Venue.jpg

summary.text: Neuschwanstein Castle is a 19th-century historicist palace on a rugged hill in the Alpine foothills of southern Bavaria, Germany, near the Austrian border. It stands in the municipality of Schwangau, above the village of Hohenschwangau.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: In the Swabia region of Bavaria, in the municipality of Schwangau; the nearest larger town is Füssen.

facts.label: Setting
facts.value: The castle stands above the narrow gorge of the Pöllat stream, east of the Alpsee and Schwansee lakes.

facts.label: Height
facts.value: According to Guinness World Records, at 65 metres it is the tallest castle in the world.

facts.label: World Heritage
facts.value: Since 2025 it has been part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site "The Palaces of King Ludwig II of Bavaria".

media.alt: Neuschwanstein Castle perched on a wooded hill in the Bavarian Alps, photographed from the Marienbrücke.
media.attribution: Thomas Wolf (www.foto-tw.de), CC BY-SA 3.0 DE, via Wikimedia Commons

summary.text: The Matterhorn is a near-symmetric pyramidal peak of the Pennine Alps on the border between Switzerland and Italy. At 4,478 metres, it is one of the highest summits in the Alps and has become an emblem of Switzerland.

facts.label: Summit elevation
facts.value: 4,478 metres (14,692 ft) above sea level.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: On the main watershed and border between Switzerland and Italy, in the Monte Rosa area of the Pennine Alps.

facts.label: Shape
facts.value: A large, near-symmetric pyramidal peak.

facts.label: Nickname
facts.value: Sometimes called the "Mountain of Mountains".

media.alt: The pyramid-shaped Matterhorn seen from the Domhütte in Valais, with its rock faces and snow-streaked ridges.
